children: Wall Street analysts issued a fresh round of upgrades and downgrades last week, with shifting views on AI’s impact on software, hardware makers’ growth prospects, and resilience to inflation. Salesforce
and Walmart
drew upgrades, while Adobe
and several technology hardware stocks faced downgrades.
Salesforce upgraded by Bank of America on enterprise AI outlook
Salesforce (CRM) was

to Buy from Underperform by Bank of America on October 12, with the brokerage raising its price target to $285 from $160. The firm said large enterprises are unlikely to replace software platforms that house their business logic, data, workflows and compliance frameworks as they adopt AI. Instead, AI adoption could deepen reliance on these systems.
The $285 price target values Salesforce

at 16 times its expected free cash flow for 2027, up from 9 times previously and above the peer average of 15 times. The brokerage cited easing concerns about AI-driven disruption, the company's AI strategy, strong free cash flow generation and the potential for revenue growth to accelerate.
Barclays downgrades Dell, HPE and NetApp as AI growth concerns mount
Dell Technologies (DELL), Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) and NetApp (NTAP) were
to Equal Weight from Overweight by Barclays on October 14. Analyst Tim Long lowered Dell's
price target to $574 from $603 and HPE's
to $77 from $83, while maintaining NetApp's
target at $219.

Barclays adopted a more cautious view of IT hardware companies exposed to enterprise spending, citing elevated valuations, revenue gains supported by higher memory prices and a lack of a meaningful AI-driven growth inflection.
HubSpot and monday.com downgraded by Barclays on delayed AI benefits
HubSpot (HUBS) and monday.com (MNDY) were
to Equal Weight from Overweight by Barclays on October 12, as the brokerage said AI-related benefits could take longer to materialize than previously expected.
Barclays maintained its price target of $240 for HubSpot
and $100 for monday.com
. For HubSpot
, the firm said its bullish thesis had relied on AI usage accelerating growth, but customer caution during the AI transition could delay that improvement. For monday.com
, analyst Raimo Lenschow said AI monetization was gaining traction but remained in its early stages, with AI ARR accounting for only 1% of total ARR and not yet offsetting a slowdown in core growth.
Deutsche Bank upgrades Walmart as inflation bolsters value proposition
Walmart

was upgraded to Buy from Hold by Deutsche Bank on October 15, with analyst Krisztina Katai raising the price target to $136 from $113. The brokerage said persistent inflation could strengthen Walmart’s value proposition and accelerate market-share gains as consumers seek lower prices.

Deutsche Bank expects margin growth from advertising, marketplace, and membership, alongside automation gains. Strong food market-share gains and e-commerce momentum also support its improved 2027 outlook.
GoDaddy downgraded by RBC as AI reshapes the web

GoDaddy (GDDY) was downgraded to Sector Perform from Outperform by RBC Capital Markets on October 12. Analyst Brad Erickson maintained his $95 price target, citing the potential impact of AI agents on the company's traditional domain, website-building and digital-commerce businesses.
RBC said the internet was shifting from static, publisher-driven pages toward AI agents that deliver results based on user intent. The brokerage also cited GoDaddy's
38% rebound from its June low, saying the rally left less room for further valuation expansion.
MongoDB stays bullish as Needham and BofA reaffirm Buy ratings

MongoDB (MDB) rose more than 6% on October 13 after Needham and Bank of America reiterated their Buy ratings on the database software company. Needham maintained its price target at $430, while BofA kept its target at $540.

Needham analyst Mike Cikos said discussions following MongoDB's Investor Day reinforced the firm's confidence in the company's go-to-market strategy, platform cross-selling opportunities, and potential to expand adoption among large customers. Bank of America analyst Koji Ikeda said MongoDB's
JSON document database remains differentiated for enterprise digital modernization and AI workloads, supporting the firm's long-term growth outlook.
Wells Fargo double downgrades Adobe, upgrades Tyler Technologies

Adobe (ADBE) was downgraded to Underweight from Overweight by Wells Fargo on October 12, with analyst Michael Turrin cutting the price target to $225 from $270. The firm cited slowing organic growth, rising AI competition and execution risks amid a management transition.

In contrast, Wells Fargo upgraded Tyler Technologies (TYL) to Overweight from Equal Weight and raised its price target to $400 from $335, citing fading booking headwinds and scope for a recovery in 2027.
Well Fargo also raised its price targets on
ServiceNow
(NOW) to $190 from $175,
Palo Alto Networks
(PANW) to $525 from $475, and
CrowdStrik
e (CRWD) to $300 from $235. It cut its target on
Figm
a (FIG) to $30 from $34.
Vertical Research upgrades Lockheed Martin on missile demand
Lockheed Martin

was upgraded to Buy from Hold by Vertical Research on October 14, with analyst Robert Stallard setting a $600 price target. Stallard expects the company’s missile business to grow about 11% annually through the end of the decade, citing demand for missile replenishment despite uncertainty over the U.S. defense budget.
